children: An investment adviser has expanded a legal malpractice lawsuit it brought against U.S. law firm King & Spalding to include another law firm, Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer, alleging that lawyers at both firms worked to wrest the ownership of a health care-based fund away from it.

White Oak Global Advisors first sued King & Spalding in New York County Supreme Court earlier this year, alleging that its former partner Terry Novetsky worked against its interests while representing the company by secretly helping Isaac Soleimani, the then-CEO of White Oak's health care-based fund.

That scheme continued when Novetsky joined Kramer Levin in early 2023, White Oak alleged in an updated version of its lawsuit filed Tuesday. New York-founded Kramer Levin merged with Herbert ​Smith Freehills, a larger firm with UK ⁠and Australian roots, in June 2025.
White Oak said King & Spalding and Kramer Levin worked on dozens of corporate matters for the company.

"The intentional misconduct of King & Spalding and HSF Kramer and their partners went far beyond garden-variety malpractice," said a spokesperson for Kasowitz LLP, which is representing White Oak. The spokesperson said the firms "actively mapped out and executed a plan intended to damage White Oak’s interests and, ultimately, to facilitate a hostile takeover of their own client."
White Oak said it is seeking at least $1 billion in damages, including at least $500 million in punitive damages.
An HSF Kramer spokesperson said in a statement that White Oak's claims are "without merit. Members of the firm acted appropriately, and we expect to prevail in court."

King & Spalding in an April 26 filing said the "vast majority of the allegations" in White Oak's complaint "have nothing to do with K&S." White Oak's claim that King & Spalding's alleged malpractice prohibited it from launching two multi-billion dollar health care funds was "patently speculative," King & Spalding said.
"For a complaint alleging $1 billion in damages, its silence on these basic facts is telling," King & Spalding said. The firm is represented by a team of attorneys from Steptoe.

The lawsuit alleges that Novetsky and the law firms, while representing White Oak Global Advisors and White Oak Healthcare, colluded with Soleimani to help him obtain control of White Oak Healthcare. White Oak alleged that Novetsky and Soleimani communicated with each other through their personal Gmail accounts.
Novetsky did not immediately respond to a request for comment. He retired from HSF Kramer in January, according to the lawsuit.

Soleimani, who is not named as a defendant in the malpractice lawsuit, was terminated as the CEO of White Oak Healthcare in September 2023. Attorneys at Mintz, Levin, Cohn, Ferris, Glovsky, and Popeo, who represented Soleimani in another legal dispute with White Oak, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
